top.title: 49ers' ‘unc package' of Mike Evans, Keenan Allen catching passes, praise
top.description: Mike Evans (5) and Keenan Allen celebrate after Evans' touchdown reception against the Minnesota Vikings in the second quarter Sunday in Mexico City. (Agustin Cuevas/Getty Images) Mike Evans and Keenan Allen played 19 snaps together in the San Francisco 49ers ' 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. On seven of those plays, Evans and Allen were the lone wideouts in a two-receiver set. According to head coach Kyle Shanahan , that's called the "unc package." "We mix in so many guys, and I know everybody's name, but when I'm thinking about football and stuff, I don't always just spit out names fast," Shanahan said. "So sometimes it's just easier for me to say unc. Everyone knows who I'm talking about." What do Evans and Allen think about the nickname? "I hope they like it," Shanahan said. "I think it's cool. They're not, like, really uncles. They're in their 30s. They're still young." Evans, 33, and Allen, 34, are in their 13th and 14th NFL seasons, respectively. One is a 6-foot-5, 231-pound one-on-one matchup nightmare who can win over the top, up the sideline or across the middle of the field. The other is a smaller-but-still-big 6-2 receiver who thrives on short and intermediate routes. Despite having different builds, they bring a handful of shared qualities to San Francisco's offense, according to Shanahan. He couldn't stop listing them Wednesday. "They're still unbelievably talented" at their ages, he said, "but just the intelligence of both of them, and just the poise they have, and how competitive they are, and how good they are at whatever you ask them to do … just how good of blockers they are, how good they are at routes that you haven't seen them run before. "It's whatever you put in, they figure out." Did Shanahan have fun scheming them open Sunday? "Yeah, big time," he said. Evans caught six passes for 109 yards and a touchdown. Allen trailed with three catches for 38 yards. There were countless plays where they worked in unison. For instance: On Evans' touchdown catch late in the second quarter, Allen directly freed him up for a one-handed grab in the back corner of the end zone. Lined up together in a condensed formation - with the ball on Minnesota's 4 - Evans ran a corner route and Allen ran a zig underneath him. Three Vikings defenders were split between the two of them. Allen occupied a double team just long enough for Evans to win his one-on-one matchup against safety Harrison Smith. Once cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. recovered to chase Evans, it was too late. He was a step behind, and Evans was in for six. top.title: Hurricanes rally past Lightning in third, 3-1
top.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: Sean Walker #26 of the Carolina Hurricanes celebrates with teammates after scoring a goal during the second period against the New York Rangers at Madison Square Garden on November 22, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jared Silber/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images The Carolina Hurricanes picked up their third win in a row and their 19th of the season with a gutsy road victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning by a 3-1 margin on the night before Thanksgiving. The Hurricanes got an exemplary performance from goaltender Brandon Bussi, who ultimately turned aside 32 of the 33 shots he faced and bought Carolina time to ultimately rally for the win in the third period. Bussi and Lightning goalie Andrei Vasilevskiy dueled to a scoreless first period before the Lightning built up a territorial advantage into the second period, when Anthony Cirelli struck just 55 seconds in on a power play goal on assists from former Hurricane Jake Guentzel and Nikita Kucherov. The Long Island native battled hard to keep the Canes down by just a goal for the duration of the second, as the Bolts mustered 7 high-danger chances in the frame. Carolina finally broke through offensively in the third period on an Eric Robinson tally when the speedy winger beat Vasilevskiy from a sharp angle after a flubbed puck and turnover by Tampa Bay defenseman Max Crozier. Just a minute and a half later, the Canes took the lead on a nice passing play when Jaccob Slavin got his first of the year by fooling Vasilevskiy into thinking a cross-ice pass was coming before depositing the puck into the suddenly-vacated portion of the goal. Sebastian Aho and Seth Jarvis picked up their 21st and 9th assists of the season on the play. Slavo shoots and he scores for the lead pic.twitter.com/fZPiJcBzLn — Carolina Hurricanes (@Canes) November 26, 2026 Carolina kept the Lightning from establishing dangerous possession in the zone as the clock wore down, and even had multiple bids to get an insurance goal at the empty net that were turned aside by some sharp impromptu goaltending from Bolts winger Brandon Hagel. Jackson Blake ultimately found the yawning cage to put the game away at 3-1. The win makes the Hurricanes the first team in the Eastern Conference to surpass the 40-point mark, but they did not extend their seven-point lead in the Metropolitan Division over the New Jersey Devils, who beat the Columbus Blue Jackets in a shootout. The Canes will be back in action again on Saturday when they host the Ottawa Senators.

top.title: Rams S Kam Kinchens ejected; Packers WR Christian Watson evaluated for concussion
top.description: (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the second quarter of the Green Bay Packers-Los Angeles Rams game, Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and leading with his helmet on a tackle attempt on Packers receiver Christian Watson. You can find video of the play below: Christian Watson gets CRUSHED and is down injured pic.twitter.com/U0etpi9e8G — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 26, 2026 Initially, a cart came out for Watson, but the receiver was able to leave the field under his own power. The Packers are currently listing Watson as questionable to return and say that he’s being evaluated for a concussion. To be honest, it looks like the biggest hit he ended up taking was when his head hit the turf on the way down, not necessarily Kinchens’ blow to Watson’s facemask. Green Bay was not awarded a first down on this play due to offsetting penalties. Packers receiver Matthew Golden was called for offensive pass interference (you can only set a pick within a yard of the line of scrimmage), so they simply replayed the fourth-and-one play. After not getting a man coverage look with their running back’s motion, like they had on the play that Watson was injured on, head coach Matt LaFleur called a timeout and elected to kick the football, setting up a 17-17 tie going into halftime. We’ll keep you updated when we hear more news on the Packers’ injury situation.

nigeria.description: Donyell Malen’s penalty gave Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, as the injury-hit reigning champions saw their perfect record in this season’s competition come to an end. The result ends PSG’s perfect record in this season’s league phase, and halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for Luis Enrique’s team. They fall two points behind Real Madrid, who are now clear at the top of the standings as the only side still with a 100 percent record after five matches. It is only a minor setback for PSG in their quest to finish in the top eight of the 36-team table, and therefore qualify directly for the last 16 without having to go through the play-off round like in the last two campaigns. But the Parisians could have done with the boost of a victory as they come to terms with the loss of the outstanding Desire Doue, who may not play again this season after rupturing the ACL in his right knee last weekend. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, another of their outstanding attacking players, recently succumbed to the same injury, while Dembele has been struggling for fitness too and PSG’s prospects of winning a third straight Champions League title are undoubtedly diminished as a result. nigeria.title: Dangote Refinery to list on Nigerian Exchange December 1
nigeria.description: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery says it will begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) Group on December 1, marking its entry into the Nigerian stock market following its initial public offering (IPO). Devakumar Edwin, vice-president of oil and gas at Dangote Group, announced the development on Wednesday, according to a Reuters report. The listing comes after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the refinery’s share allocation plan following its heavily oversubscribed IPO, which closed last month. The regulatory approval cleared the way for the company to distribute shares to investors and proceed with preparations for its stock market debut. The refinery had earlier sought to increase the size of its IPO by up to 30 per cent to approximately $2.1 billion following strong investor demand. On September 11, Aliko Dangote, president of Dangote Industries Limited (DIL), said the refinery planned to pursue a listing on a United States stock exchange after expanding its production capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day within the next two and a half years. However, on November 8, Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s IPO fell short of its target of attracting 10 million investors. Despite missing the target, Africa’s richest person said the offer attracted “millions of investors”. He described the level of participation as significant when compared with some of the largest public offerings in Africa and globally. nigeria.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
nigeria.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. nigeria.title: ‘Five bullets’ — NDC supporter recounts attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team in Delta
nigeria.description: A supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has recounted how gunmen allegedly shot him five times during an attack on the campaign team of Ovie Omo-Agege, the party’s candidate for Delta Central, in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The survivor, who sustained gunshot injuries to his chest and mouth, narrated his ordeal in a video shared on the NDC’s X page on Wednesday. The video showed him speaking from his hospital bed during a visit by Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, its vice-presidential candidate, to survivors of the attack. Recounting events leading up to the shooting, the man said he had received threats after participating in a 10,000-man march organised by the NDC in Delta State. According to him, his wife received a telephone call from individuals who threatened to shut down his business. “To be very precise, on Sunday, when we were in church, in the early hours of the day, they went and sealed the whole business premises. I could not get access to the premises; I could not offload my goods,” he recalled. “A week later, my truck that brought goods from Lagos, they seized the truck and drove it to the local government secretariat.” He said the truck was detained for more than four days, adding that no explanation had been provided for its seizure. The supporter said the attack occurred on Monday while Omo-Agege was addressing supporters at the campaign venue, when gunmen stormed the gathering and opened fire. He said one of the attackers called out his name before shooting him as he attempted to escape towards his car. “One of them started shouting, ‘That is Agba, shoot Agba, that is Agba, look at Agba going.’ Before I could say Jack, the gunshot came straight to my chest,” he said. “There is a bullet here, through the throat. There is a bullet here…five bullets on the chest and the mouth. “So, the target was just to kill me, but to God be the glory, I’m alive.” He attributed the attack to his political affiliation and support for the NDC’s presidential and vice-presidential candidates. “The whole thing is because I’m supporting NDC; I’m supporting Obi and Kwankwaso,” he said. Another survivor receiving treatment at the hospital also expressed determination to continue supporting the party despite the violence. “No matter the number of persons they shoot or attempt to kill in their time, Peter Obi will become president, Rabiu Kwankwaso will become vice-president, and Nigeria will be okay,” he said. Recall in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Nigeria Police Force spokesperson, Ani Iniedu, said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed and several others injured during the attack. nigeria.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once. The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history. The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig. Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won. South Africa: three wins South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown. Namibia: one win Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990. Botswana: one win Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page. Angola: one win Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe. nigeria.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win
nigeria.description: Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish. Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions as they triumphed in Azerbaijan at the Baku Olympic stadium. The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League. Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal. Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence. Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork. Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path. The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player. Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval. The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way. It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him. Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header. Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another. Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him. Adeyemi crashed a shot off the bar as Barcelona threatened sporadically in the final stages without adding to their already ample tally. nigeria.title: 2027 election: Why attack NDC if Obi has no path to victory? Akpata asks
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain Olumide Akpata says the party believes its presidential candidate Peter Obi has a path to victory in 2027 and should be allowed to campaign without intimidation. Akpata spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday while reacting to political violence in Edo State. On Wednesday, the Edo State Police Command confirmed that gunmen opened fire on supporters gathered along Airport Road to welcome Obi to Benin City, leaving one person injured. “Everyone is entitled to their own permutations. You know, everyone is entitled to their own back-of-the-envelope calculations regarding what the outcome will be, right? Which general goes to war without first counting the cost, as the good book says? So, for me personally, indeed, for those of us in the NDC, our permutations would seem to suggest that there is indeed a pathway,” Akpata said. Questioning the APC’s confidence ahead of the election, the former president of the Nigerian Bar Association asked why the NDC was being prevented from campaigning if it had no prospect of winning. “If you are that confident, why are your minions and why are those who are acting on your behalf making it difficult for the NDC to campaign? If you are that confident that there’s no pathway, why not leave us to what you consider to be our folly? Leave us alone. Let us continue to delude ourselves. Let us stay where we are. We are fine with that,” he said. “But why come after us? Why attack my office? Why shoot Senator Omo-Agege? If you are so confident that there’s no pathway for us, let us be.” Akpata also said the NDC received advance intelligence that armed individuals planned to infiltrate its town hall meeting. “We got intel this morning that the plan was for some individuals to infiltrate our town hall meeting and come in with attire, with our old NDC caps and T-shirts, and then cause mayhem. Come in armed and cause mayhem,” he said. He added that the warning was shared with security agencies after friends and family in Benin City also contacted him with concerns. “I got the intel. Quite a number of other persons got it. A lot of my friends and family in Benin City who had received this information called me out of concern, understandably so. So we had to escalate. We had to send the information to the police. We had to send the information to the State Security Service and all of that,” he said. According to Akpata, the planned disruption did not occur inside the town hall meeting. “At the town hall meeting, no such thing happened.” The legal practitioner alleged that the party’s office was attacked after NDC members had left, and said the attack was intended to intimidate them into abandoning the campaign. “They knew we had left the office. nigeria.title: Nigeria needs experienced, courageous leaders to tackle challenges, Amaechi hails Atiku at 80
nigeria.description: Former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, saying Nigeria needs leaders with the experience, courage and capacity to address its economic and security challenges. Amaechi, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, described Atiku as a distinguished statesman, entrepreneur, philanthropist and patriot whose contributions to Nigeria’s political, economic and social development remained significant. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), turned 80 on Wednesday. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State, recalled Atiku’s tenure as Vice President between 1999 and 2007, noting his role in consolidating the Fourth Republic and driving economic reforms. He also highlighted Atiku’s leadership of the National Council on Privatisation, saying his contributions reflected his belief in private-sector development and an enabling business environment. The former minister also commended Atiku’s entrepreneurial investments in agriculture, logistics and real estate, as well as his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola. He said the university reflected Atiku’s commitment to education and human capital development. Amaechi further acknowledged Atiku’s philanthropic activities, particularly his support for educational opportunities for disadvantaged Nigerians and young people affected by the Chibok tragedy. Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, Amaechi said Nigeria required leadership capable of restoring economic confidence, strengthening national security, improving education and healthcare, and ensuring reliable electricity supply. He also backed Atiku’s proposed reintroduction of petroleum production subsidy, arguing that the policy could reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices on households. According to Amaechi, Nigeria needs a people-centred development agenda that prioritises entrepreneurship, technological innovation, human capital development and private-sector-led growth. He expressed confidence in Atiku’s ambition to contest the 2027 presidential election, saying the country needed leaders who understood its challenges and were prepared to take difficult decisions. Amaechi also called for a Nigeria where young people could find opportunities at home, farmers could prosper, businesses could grow and citizens could access quality education regardless of their backgrounds. He wished Atiku good health, wisdom and strength, while commending his contributions to public service, education, philanthropy and the country’s democratic development. “At 80, your journey is not merely a story of past accomplishments but a reminder that experience must be deployed in the service of the future,” Amaechi said. Saraki made the call following allegations that the governor had summoned some traditional rulers to Ilorin and threatened to suspend those who received leaders of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during courtesy visits to their palaces. In a statement personally signed by him, Saraki said the alleged actions followed his stakeholder engagements in Kwara North Senatorial District, which began last week. He explained that visits to traditional rulers were part of established customs and protocols, adding that the royal fathers should be allowed to receive political leaders regardless of their party affiliations. Saraki said traditional rulers were fathers of all and should not be subjected to pressure over their interactions with politicians. He also urged the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to caution Abdulrazaq, saying political differences should not prevent opposition parties from engaging communities and traditional institutions. The former Senate President recalled that during the 16 years the PDP governed Kwara State, traditional rulers were not prevented from receiving opposition leaders. He said democracy required tolerance of opposing views and urged the governor to respect the state’s traditional institutions. Saraki, however, insisted that the alleged actions would not discourage the PDP from continuing its engagements across the state. He said the party would sustain its outreach to communities in the three senatorial districts, adding that the response to its engagements had been encouraging. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. Changes from Begich’s original version The committee rewrote the bill before reporting it. Begich’s introduced text asked Treasury and Commerce to study funding bitcoin purchases with surplus remittances from Federal Reserve Banks or a revaluation of the Fed’s gold certificates, as well as with tax payments, tariff revenue and gifts. Those options are gone from the amended study, which now looks at swapping other digital assets in the stockpile, forfeitures and settlements, and partnerships with states or private entities. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. sports.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: Sean Walker #26 of the Carolina Hurricanes celebrates with teammates after scoring a goal during the second period against the New York Rangers at Madison Square Garden on November 22, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jared Silber/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images The Carolina Hurricanes picked up their third win in a row and their 19th of the season with a gutsy road victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning by a 3-1 margin on the night before Thanksgiving. The Hurricanes got an exemplary performance from goaltender Brandon Bussi, who ultimately turned aside 32 of the 33 shots he faced and bought Carolina time to ultimately rally for the win in the third period. Bussi and Lightning goalie Andrei Vasilevskiy dueled to a scoreless first period before the Lightning built up a territorial advantage into the second period, when Anthony Cirelli struck just 55 seconds in on a power play goal on assists from former Hurricane Jake Guentzel and Nikita Kucherov. The Long Island native battled hard to keep the Canes down by just a goal for the duration of the second, as the Bolts mustered 7 high-danger chances in the frame. Carolina finally broke through offensively in the third period on an Eric Robinson tally when the speedy winger beat Vasilevskiy from a sharp angle after a flubbed puck and turnover by Tampa Bay defenseman Max Crozier. Just a minute and a half later, the Canes took the lead on a nice passing play when Jaccob Slavin got his first of the year by fooling Vasilevskiy into thinking a cross-ice pass was coming before depositing the puck into the suddenly-vacated portion of the goal. Sebastian Aho and Seth Jarvis picked up their 21st and 9th assists of the season on the play. Slavo shoots and he scores for the lead pic.twitter.com/fZPiJcBzLn — Carolina Hurricanes (@Canes) November 26, 2026 Carolina kept the Lightning from establishing dangerous possession in the zone as the clock wore down, and even had multiple bids to get an insurance goal at the empty net that were turned aside by some sharp impromptu goaltending from Bolts winger Brandon Hagel. Jackson Blake ultimately found the yawning cage to put the game away at 3-1. The win makes the Hurricanes the first team in the Eastern Conference to surpass the 40-point mark, but they did not extend their seven-point lead in the Metropolitan Division over the New Jersey Devils, who beat the Columbus Blue Jackets in a shootout. The Canes will be back in action again on Saturday when they host the Ottawa Senators.

sports.title: Rams S Kam Kinchens ejected; Packers WR Christian Watson evaluated for concussion
sports.description: (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the second quarter of the Green Bay Packers-Los Angeles Rams game, Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and leading with his helmet on a tackle attempt on Packers receiver Christian Watson. You can find video of the play below: Christian Watson gets CRUSHED and is down injured pic.twitter.com/U0etpi9e8G — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 26, 2026 Initially, a cart came out for Watson, but the receiver was able to leave the field under his own power. The Packers are currently listing Watson as questionable to return and say that he’s being evaluated for a concussion. To be honest, it looks like the biggest hit he ended up taking was when his head hit the turf on the way down, not necessarily Kinchens’ blow to Watson’s facemask. Green Bay was not awarded a first down on this play due to offsetting penalties. Packers receiver Matthew Golden was called for offensive pass interference (you can only set a pick within a yard of the line of scrimmage), so they simply replayed the fourth-and-one play. After not getting a man coverage look with their running back’s motion, like they had on the play that Watson was injured on, head coach Matt LaFleur called a timeout and elected to kick the football, setting up a 17-17 tie going into halftime. We’ll keep you updated when we hear more news on the Packers’ injury situation.

sports.title: ‘Prepared to throw it no times’: Joe Burrow ready to get extreme if he has to
sports.description: Cincinnati Bengals Joe Burrow takes questions from media during a press conference after practice at Paycor Stadium, Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026, in downtown Cincinnati. The Cincinnati Bengals lost 22-20 to the Washington Commanders on Monday night in a game that many expected them to roll and pull away from the rest of the AFC North. The Bengals have been extremely pass-happy this season, and while it’s been largely beneficial, Monday’s loss highlighted the sort of issues that might surface down the stretch if the offense doesn’t find more balance. During his media availability on Wednesday, Burrow was asked if he felt the team needed to commit to the run more. It depends,” Burrow answered. “Obviously, you’d love to be super explosive in both. But we’ll play the game however we need to play to win it. And I’m certainly prepared for either one. I’m prepared to throw it no times. I’m prepared to throw it 70 times. Whatever it takes to win.” Joe Burrow when asked whether the Bengals need to run the ball more or more effectively over the rest of the season: “I’m prepared to throw it zero times. I’m prepared to throw it 70 times, whatever it takes to win.” #Bengals https://t.co/i6ahCl5vPx — Chatterbox Sports (@CBoxSports) November 25, 2026 After the Bengals scored in the third quarter, they only ran the ball twice more in the game. Running back Samaje Perine finished with only six carries for 26 yards and the team finished with just 36 yards rushing in total. Cincinnati is averaging just 79.4 rushing yards a game, third-fewest in the league this season. Cincinnati’s next game is against the New Orleans Saints, and Burrow knows that with the skill set of the Saints’ defense, his squad will have to adjust. “Their linebackers are good at blitzing,” Burrow said about New Orleans. “Their front is explosive, and they’re good rushers. When you put those two things in combination, it makes it hard. Just worried about trying to win this week. Landscape will play out the way it plays out, and we just got to keep winning.” If Cincinnati can’t run the ball against good defensive fronts, teams with good rushers like the Saints will be able to tee off on Burrow, and Cincinnati could find the momentum out of its sails fast. Burrow says he’s willing to do whatever it takes to win. Sunday’s game will be a great opportunity to see if he can prove that by following the gameplan. Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Ben Casparius will miss the entire 2027 season after undergoing elbow surgery, the team announced Wednesday. “Los Angeles Dodger right-handed pitcher Ben Casparius had right elbow UCL reconstruction surgery today performed by Dr. Neal ElAttrache. Casparius will miss the 2027 season.” Casparius has potential but he’s dealt with injury concerns in the past . He will work hard to return. It’s certainly an unfortunate blow, but it is worth mentioning that the MLB season could end up being shortened this year depending on how long it takes for MLB and the MLBPA to agree to a new collective bargaining agreement. Baseball fans are hopeful that the season will begin as scheduled in late March, but a lockout is expected to begin in early December at the very least. With the league and players’ association still far apart on the subject of a salary cap, there is no telling how long the expected lockout will last. In any case, Ben Casparius will work to recover and return for the 2028 season. Although he won’t pitch in 2027, it’s unclear exactly how many big league games he will miss given the uncertainty around the lockout situation. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. technology.description: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems. The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords. The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers , targeted more than 100 water systems , with incidents reported across at least 12 states , and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers . Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

science.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? science.description: null When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. science.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
science.description: null Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. science.title: AI’s stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it
science.description: MARK SYKES/SPL/Alamy There is a story, possibly apocryphal, that when the mathematician G. H. Hardy was about to undertake a dangerous sea voyage, he sent a postcard to a colleague declaring “I have solved the Riemann hypothesis”. Hardy, a staunch atheist, joked that this would prevent his ship from sinking, as God would never let him claim the credit for such a major result without revealing the details of his proof. Hardy would probably be both astonished and aghast that we now have what seems to be a proof of the Riemann hypothesis , a problem that has vexed mathematicians since the 19th century, but that no one yet understands it. The consensus among mathematicians is that the proof, produced with the aid of AI, will hold, but that it will take much more work to make it comprehensible to humans. However you feel about AI, this is a watershed moment, and one that demonstrates just how little we still understand about the capabilities of the technology. As recently as last month, leading mathematician Terence Tao speculated that AI would eventually solve the Riemann hypothesis, but that it may not happen before 2050. Now, some mathematicians are considering whether their hardest and most infamous remaining problems could be settled within months. In a year that has left mathematicians reeling, this may be the knock-out blow. Advertisement This is a watershed moment, and it shows just how little we understand about AI’s abilities For non-mathematicians, the fall of the Riemann hypothesis is harder to interpret. In the past year, AI has seen incredible advances in both maths and coding, but it is perhaps no coincidence that in these arenas, with nothing more than computer code, answers can swiftly be checked and iterated upon, allowing for rapid improvement. When it comes to other human endeavours though, from art to zoology, such verification is far harder, involving either the messy physical world, or unknowable human taste – or both. Whether this verification gap can be closed may become the biggest question of our age. Answers on a postcard, please. What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental? It has been called the hardest problem in mathematics, and now through a combination of human ingenuity and relentlessness, and the computational power of AI, the Riemann hypothesis may have finally been solved

science.title: Is The Time Traveler’s Wife the perfect audiobook to experience on shuffle?
science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Reader Jenny Ozanne writes to tell us of a horrific incident that befell her partner. He had bought Audrey Niffenegger’s novel The Time Traveler’s Wife as a CD audiobook, to listen to on long car journeys. “After a while, he complained that the plot was completely impossible to follow,” writes Jenny. “It was only when I checked his player that I realized he had accidentally set the CD to ‘shuffle’. “ Advertisement Jenny raises two points, which Feedback heartily endorses: “I’m still not sure what’s more impressive: the story’s ability to survive total chronological chaos, or the fact that he listened to three random chapters before suspecting anything was wrong.” Feedback would suggest that The Time Traveler’s Wife might be the ideal novel to experience on shuffle, since the narrative is heavily non-linear. The main character hops uncontrollably back and forth through history. This led us to wonder: would any similarly chrono-displaced stories survive the experience of being played on shuffle, or even be improved by it? We wondered, for instance, about David Mitchell’s Cloud Atlas . This has six stories set in different periods, including a future in which human clones are used as cheap labour, and a more distant future in which everything has gone a bit Mad Max . The stories are linked by characters in later timelines reading about the earlier ones, and by subtle coincidences. What would it be like on shuffle? However, after careful reflection, we realised there is only one correct answer to this, and that is Shane Carruth’s 2004 film Primer , which tells the story of two tech bros who invent a time machine in their garage. At first, they use it to go back in time and make money on the stock exchange, only to become caught up in an escalating web of betrayal and deception as they endlessly rewrite their lives. Primer is so overcomplicated, so mind-wreckingly confusing, that some poor soul once went so far as to draw a diagram trying to convey its timeline. Posted on Reddit by u/Clawz114, the diagram looks like a cross between a metro map and a flowchart of the inner workings of a chemical factory. It is therefore possible that playing the scenes in random order might actually cause the film to make more sense. science.title: ‘Blade Runner 2099’ cast praise the incredible set designs that brought the sci-fi universe to life: ‘it was all so well-realized’ (interview)
science.description: null Prime Video’s " Blade Runner 2099 " has arrived with an 8-episode limited series revealing what the "Blade Runner" world looks like 50 years after the events of director Denis Villeneuve’s "Blade Runner 2049." The most obvious change in this depressing dystopia is that replicants are running the LA show after some unmentionable ecological disaster and humans are now the ones relegated to underclass citizens. Starring Michelle Yeoh as a replicant cop named Olwen whose life clock is running out and Hunter Schafer as Cora, a desperate human posing as a replicant blade runner, "Blade Runner 2099" unties these two in a mystery revolving around a rogue blade runner and a deadly secret that might cause their city to implode. We connected with three of the sci-fi show’s main co-stars, Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon"), Lewis Gribben ("T2 Trainspotting") and Dimitri Abold ("Love Addicts") to hear more about working with creator/showrunner Silka Louisa, and immersing themselves in " Blade Runner 2099's " vivid futuristic worldbuilding. "For me it's a lot simpler than egos because he's such a goal-oriented person and all of his stuff has such a police procedural quality to it," Needham tells SPACE regarding his role as Yahya, an emotionless replicant who despises all humans. "It was really fun to just follow what Silka [Louisa] did. She wrote this great, really exciting mystery thriller, and I just got to play in that.” Matthew Needham and Hunter Schafer star in "Blade Runner 2099" (Image credit: Amazon Prime Video) Scottish actor Gribben portrays Cora's ailing younger brother Elias, who has compromised mobility and a rocky relationship with his overprotective sister. "I've played a few characters that were fairly vulnerable or insular," he notes. "Then seeing the journey of this character grow in strength and confidence and feel like becoming his own man was so compelling to me. It’s almost a relationship that falls apart between brother and sister, and that's fascinating to me because that’s such a cool dynamic you don’t always really see in television shows. That was quite interesting and made me want to try and be in it." (Image credit: Amazon Prime Video) As Bebeto, a doctor, veteran of the replicants vs. humans war, and a black-market dealer helping his species procure IDs and passports off-world, Abold enjoyed exploring the many facets of his character. "Much like Matthew and Lewis, for me it was the journey that Bebeto goes on," Abold adds. "Starting out as someone who’s so hopeful and has to try and scrape up the last dregs of hope as things start falling apart. Being subject to circumstances like that inherently make for an interesting story arc and story in general. Throwing myself into that, especially after how well Silka crafted the story and script, was something I was totally ready for." science.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
science.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Strawberries (left) grown in the Space Life Sciences Lab’s controlled environment chamber. Cucumbers (center) and lemon basil (right) grown in a controlled environment chamber at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. NASA Recent testing points to strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as potential options for future explorers. Space crops can absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water. These capabilities will become increasingly important as crewed missions extend farther from our home planet. While space crop research advances on Earth, capabilities are also expanding in space. A new investigation from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division is set to launch to the International Space Station, where the first-of-its-kind prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing crop production systems that could grow crops like these for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Sweet space strawberries Strawberries are among the few sweet fruits under consideration for spaceflight and are nutritious, aromatic, and self-pollinating. Researchers at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida are growing strawberries in flight-like growth chambers to evaluate the potential space crop, and NASA partners at The Australian Research Council Centre for Excellence in Plants for Space also are helping expand knowledge of space strawberries. Researchers at NASA Kennedy, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Western Australia recently tested a wild strawberry against NASA’s leading strawberry candidate, ‘Delizz,’ to see which thrived better under simulated space conditions. Delizz and the wild strawberry produced very different fruits, according to a study published in September in the journal Life Sciences in Space Research. Delizz grew large, red fruit, while the wild strawberry produced small, yellow fruit due to a recessive genetic mutation. But looks are not everything. When grown from a seed, the wild strawberry produced twice as many buds, flowers, and fruit as Delizz. Ultimately, however, NASA’s pick kept its top spot, as the wild strawberry grew too many runners that would take up valuable room aboard a spacecraft. Cucumbers show promise Many crops have been grown in space, but none so far have come from the gourd family. Cucumbers could be the first. Before crops like cucumbers can be grown and eaten in space, they must undergo extensive testing. NASA-funded researchers recently evaluated cucumbers for their growth, yield, and nutrition under spaceflight conditions. science.title: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)
science.description: null For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 . Ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later. Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May . Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments. "Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today . The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year. Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995. Another look at the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 astronauts aboard Tiangong on Nov. 25, 2026. (Image credit: CMSA) Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023. Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China plans to expand Tiangong , which is currently about 20% as massive as the International Space Station .

science.title: Hera spacecraft gets 1st up-close look at stadium-sized hole punched in asteroid by NASA DART mission
science.description: null NASA's DART Earth-defense mission punched a stadium-sized hole in a distant asteroid, and we have seen it up close for the first time thanks to the Hera spacecraft. NASA's DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) mission made history on Sept. 26, 2022, when it slammed into Dimorphos , the small moonlet of the much larger asteroid Didymos . The mission tested if such an impact could be deployed to divert an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Scientists have known for some time that this deflection attempt was successful; the system's orbit around the sun was lengthened by 33 minutes, but the European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera mission launched in October 2024 to travel the 120 million miles (194 million kilometers) to the Didymos system to observe the effect of the DART impact in greater detail. Now, the spacecraft has revealed that DART flattened one face of Dimorphos with a stadium-sized crater and set it tumbling chaotically. The impact also appears to have blasted out hundreds of previously unknown boulders that are now circling the binary asteroids. "Scientists debated whether Dimorphos had sustained an impact crater, changed its shape, or stayed the same," Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at the Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, said in a statement. "Much to our surprise, the answer turns out to be all three at once! The face struck by DART has been flattened into an impact crater the size of a sports stadium, which extends across the asteroid's entire width." An important step for Earth defence Michael Kueppers, ESA's Hera mission scientist, detailed some of the changes to the impacted moonlet seen by the spacecraft: "As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit. "Another big surprise is that Hera is showing that the asteroids are surrounded by hundreds of orbiting boulders, just a few meters in size." It wasn't all change for Dimorphos. Hera discovered that the boulder fields covering the regions of the moonlet not impacted look just like they did when DART imaged it in 2022. (Left) Didymos system seen by DART in 2022 (Right): the same system seen by Hera in 2026 (Image credit: ESA/NASA) Hera isn't finished with Didymos and its moonlet. The ESA spacecraft is currently in a rectangular orbit around the asteroid binary system, using its thrusters to maintain a distance of around 18.6 miles (30 kilometers). This allows Hera to continue observing Didymos and Dimorphos. Hera will soon come to within around 8 miles (13 km) of the asteroids, capturing even more detailed images of the space rocks. Following this, it will deploy two showbox-sized CubeSats , which will get even closer to the asteroids. science.title: Childhood, Career Come Full Circle for Budget Analyst at NASA Goddard
science.description: Conversations about NASA were the norm around the dinner table during Ashley Knight’s childhood. Her parents worked at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, and discussions about happenings at the agency continued even when they came home from the office. “I remember a poignant dialogue we had after the space shuttle Challenger disaster,” Knight recalled. “However, we talked just as much about the engaging work my parents were doing inside Goddard’s gates.” Her father Lyle Knight was a mechanical engineer, while her mother Julia Knight worked the bulk of her career in human resources. They brought their daughter on center for Take Your Child to Work Day and other events, and over time she became hooked. “I saw the chambers where spacecraft and instruments were being tested, as well as other facilities used to help further space exploration. Above all, I witnessed the passion and collaborative spirit everyone had at Goddard,” Knight said. “As a child, I found it incredibly fascinating.” Ashley Knight (right) on a visit to NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Md., while her parents were employees. Photo courtesy of Ashley Knight It all came full circle in late August when, after growing up around NASA and later working several contractor roles for the agency, Knight and a number of her colleagues in the Goddard Office of the Chief Financial Officer were sworn in as federal employees as part of a workforce directive to strengthen the agency’s technical core competencies by bringing mission-critical positions into the civil service. She began her Goddard career more than two decades ago following graduation from the University of Maryland in nearby College Park. As the job search began after commencement, one organization inevitably stood out, along with one particular mission. When she came across a contractor job opening at Goddard in support of the Hubble Space Telescope team, Knight jumped at the opportunity. “Hubble was doing amazing things, and I always admired how they fixed the faulty mirror,” she said, referring to how astronauts and team members corrected an early spherical aberration during the observatory’s first servicing mission. “It was exciting to become involved with such a flagship mission, especially coming right out of college.” As a project support analyst, Knight assisted engineers with test plans, data gathering, and hardware procurement for Hubble’s fifth and final shuttle servicing mission. science.title: NASA sends planes to monitor US Army's lead detonation. 'Irresponsible' to compare it to Chernobyl, agency chief says
science.description: null NASA has sent three different research aircraft and is using a satellite-based instrument to support the U.S. Army's detonation of degraded explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, the agency announced yesterday (Nov. 24). After a week-long delay caused by public concern over the event creating clouds of lead and toxic materials, today (Nov. 25) around 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT) the U.S. Army has planned to execute a controlled detonation of five tons of aging explosives at the ammunition plant. The detonation follows concerns that cooling winter temperatures or attempts to chemically neutralize the materials could lead to an unexpected, uncontrolled explosion. "In challenging circumstances such as this, you want the nation's best on the field. That is precisely why you call on NASA , putting our airborne and space-based sensors and some of the brightest scientific minds in the country to work," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in an online statement . To support this detonation, NASA deployed three research aircraft : a P-3 Orion, a Gulfstream III from NASA's Langley Research Center and a B200 from NASA Ames. The agency is also monitoring the situation using its TEMPO (Tropospheric Emissions: Monitoring of Pollution) instrument which is mounted and orbiting Earth on a commercial satellite. "Working alongside our partners across the federal government, NASA is utilizing its advanced scientific instruments and expertise to collect environmental and atmospheric data to inform the broader federal response," NASA stated . The environmental monitoring using TEMPO is especially important as the materials to be detonated include lead azide and other toxic components that are causing not just environmental worries, but significant local concern over possible health repercussions. This concern is severe enough that, following detonation, officials are encouraging local residents to stay indoors with the doors and windows closed for 24-28 hours. In fact, the CDC has activated an emergency response "to provide accurate public health communication and technical assistance," the CDC stated online . They have also offered additional guidance for locals to try and mitigate as much exposure to toxic materials like lead dust as possible. science.title: Eye of the Sahara
science.description: NASA/Luke Delaney The Richat Structure, also known as the “Eye of the Sahara,” is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026. It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years old created by igneous activity and uplift in the nation of Mauritania. In this type of geologic structure, rocks exposed in the center of the “bullseye” are older than rocks forming the outer rings. This structure measures 45 kilometers (28 miles) across and is made up of igneous and sedimentary rocks. Image credit: NASA/Luke Delaney

science.title: Satellites watch volcanic eruptions add new beaches on Iwo Jima | Space photo of the day for Nov. 25, 2026
science.description: null Iwo Jima on Oct. 26, 2026 on the left and the same location on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the impact of a volcanic eruption. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey ) Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches. What is it? On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak. When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11. The island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind. And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches. Why is it incredible? On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of new land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption. This is not the first time that a volcano has created new land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case. But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and quickly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023 . And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land. "I imagine we'll see this new land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement . "But we'll have to wait and see."

The images focus on an area of sky toward the galactic bulge, a densely packed, spherical region of stars that surrounds the center of a galaxy’s disk. These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy. Astronomers study the Milky Way’s galactic bulge because it holds nearly a quarter of the galaxy’s stellar mass, and its proximity allows them to examine the region in greater detail. Although we can see the glow from these crowded spheres of stars in other galaxies, they are too jam-packed and far away to resolve individual stars. By studying the Milky Way’s galactic bulge, researchers hope to find new planets and better understand how galaxies form, evolve, and interact over billions of years.
